tagline: A tiny neural network you can read, train in the browser, and export to ONNX.
short_description: A hand-written Rust neural network compiled to WebAssembly: forward pass, backprop, SGD, and a ~200-line protobuf encoder that exports ONNX—with every weight, gradient, and loss step rendered on screen.
long_description: TROT (Transparent Rust ONNX Trainer) is a small neural network built to be inspected rather than trusted. The model, backpropagation, loss, and weight updates are plain Rust loops in trot-core—no ndarray, no autodiff—compiled to WebAssembly so training runs entirely in the browser with no server, Python, or install. Six panels expose the whole pipeline: train with selectable activations and optional L2, export a hand-encoded ONNX graph and verify it with an in-place onnxruntime-web round-trip, browse the deterministic generated corpus (including intentionally flipped labels), inspect the full W1/b1/W2 weight grids, read the last minibatch's gradients cell by cell, and trace a single prediction through z1, activation, z2, and sigmoid. The corpus is a deterministic function of seed and size over a fixed 50-token grammar, so there is no dataset blob, and every number on the page is generated live.
notes: Custom domain trot.livive.net from CNAME; GitHub Pages also serves the repo path. The committed trot.wasm keeps the static site runnable without a Rust toolchain. CI covers unit/gradient/determinism tests, corpus audits, the activation x L2 matrix, a wasm ABI smoke test, and ONNX round-trip validation.

how_to_play.title: 1. Train a network you can read
how_to_play.body: Pick an activation, corpus size, learning rate, batch size, and label-noise rate. The page boots with a 300-step run, then shows the BCE + penalty decomposition and the loss curve as it trains.

how_to_play.title: 2. Inspect every number
how_to_play.body: Open the Weights and Gradients panels to see W1, b1, W2, and the last minibatch's dW1/db1/dW2/db2. Trace a prediction token by token through z1, h, z2, and sigmoid.

how_to_play.title: 3. Export and verify ONNX
how_to_play.body: The Export panel writes a four-node opset-13 ONNX graph with a hand-rolled protobuf encoder, then loads the bytes into onnxruntime-web and compares every test prediction against the in-browser model.
